Subject: Proposal to begin a performance support plan for Michael Grant

Hi Laura / Marissa,

I want to start the conversation about initiating a formal performance support pathway for Michael Grant (Product Analytics). Over the past quarter I've documented repeated missed milestones and several missed 1:1 commitments despite coaching. I have attached my observation notes and a first-pass draft PIP that leans on the HR template.

Key context:
- Role: Product Analytics (individual contributor)
- Main gaps: timeliness on deliverables, lack of proactive communication with partners, and recurring quality issues in data pipelines
- Timeline: three-month support plan with weekly 1:1 checkpoints and milestone deliverables

Before I share anything with Michael, I want HR and legal to confirm the wording and compliance/risks. Can you confirm next steps and whether we should include an external HR consultant? I’ve cc'd Neha for legal visibility.

Attachments: manager_observation_notes_2026-11.pdf, PIP_Draft_Michael_Grant_v1.docx

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal to begin a performance support plan for Michael Grant

Vanessa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. I reviewed the manager notes and the PIP draft. HR checklist next steps:

1) Align on objectives and measurable success criteria (I added comments in HR_PIP_Template_v3.docx).
2) Confirm reasonable accommodations and document any prior informal coaching offered.
3) Confirm the 1:1 cadence and attendee list for weekly check-ins (manager + employee + HR as needed).
4) If termination is a possible outcome, request Legal review of wording to avoid ambiguity.

I recommend we loop in an external consultant for the first kickoff meeting to ensure consistency across sensitive language; happy to introduce Harper Consulting (copied).

I will redline the template and return a consolidated PIP draft by end of day Friday so we can get legal sign-off.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Draft PIP for legal review (please prioritize)

Neha / Laura —

Attaching the consolidated draft (PIP_Draft_Michael_Grant_v1.docx) with my manager notes embedded. This is time-sensitive; Michael's quarterly review window closes mid-December and I'd like to start the support plan the week of Dec 13 if HR and legal agree.

Specific asks for legal:
- Flag any language that might be interpreted as punitive rather than corrective.
- Confirm we’re compliant with leave/ADA/termination notice rules.
- Suggest alternative phrasing for the "possible next steps" section.

If it helps, I can redact the "possible next steps" section for the shared version to the employee pending legal OK.

Thanks,
Vanessa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, external-legal@crockerpartners.com
Date: 2026-12-04T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft PIP for legal review (please prioritize)

Vanessa / Laura —

Thanks for the draft. I reviewed and have the following high-level recommendations:

1) Tone & remedies: Recast a few statements that read as restorative (good) but could be read as presumptive of termination. E.g., change "failure to meet these milestones will lead to termination" to "a failure to meet the agreed milestones may result in further corrective or disciplinary actions, up to and including termination."
2) ADA / accommodation: Add a short paragraph that documents the employee's right to request reasonable accommodations and how those requests will be handled; do not tie accommodation requests to timelines.
3) Documentation & retention: We should track the check-ins in the HR case file; remove language that mandates permanent inclusion of manager notes in public records.
4) Sign-off flow: Legal asks that HR be the primary owner of the final PIP document and that the manager uses the HR-approved version to share with the employee.

I’ve added inline comments in the attached file and flagged two clauses for removal. If Harper Consulting will be involved in the kickoff meeting, ensure they sign an NDA or only attend as observers — we do not want unvetted external participants in disciplinary conversations.

I can do a final pass on Monday.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Employment Law
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft PIP for legal review (please prioritize)

Laura / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I’ve accepted the legal wording and adjusted the draft per Neha’s guidance (removed the explicit termination phrasing and added the accommodations paragraph). Attached is the version HR-approved for sharing.

Next steps:
- Laura: please confirm HR will own distribution and the kickoff cadence.
- Neha: final legal sign-off when you have a chance; otherwise Laura has approval to proceed.

If all good, I plan to schedule the initial conversation with Michael on Dec 8 at 2:00pm PT and attach the PIP. If anyone prefers to attend, please let me know; HR presence would be my preference.

Attachments: HR_PIP_Template_v3.docx, PIP_Draft_Michael_Grant_v1.docx

—Vanessa
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Performance support plan kickoff and next steps

Hi Michael,

Following our informal coaching conversations, I want to formalize a short-term performance support plan to help you get back on track. Attached is the support plan that outlines clear objectives, success criteria, and weekly checkpoints. Key points:

- Duration: 12 weeks with weekly 1:1s to review progress and provide coaching
- Objectives: deliverables, quality standards for pipeline changes, and communication expectations with cross-functional partners
- Support: I will provide direct coaching and Laura is available for HR support; we will also accommodate any reasonable requests you raise.

Please review the attached document before our kickoff meeting tomorrow, Dec 9 at 10:00am PT. The intent of this plan is corrective and supportive — the goal is to give you clear expectations and an opportunity to succeed.

Attachments: PIP_Draft_Michael_Grant_v1.docx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Management
